data.name: v2.22.0: Node.js 22 Required, Export Customers, Multiple Payment Accounts
data.body:
<!--

![v2.22.0](https://res.cloudinary.com/dza7lstvk/image/upload/v1792580034/Releases/v2-22-0-e8c8a3.png)

# v2.22.0: Node.js 22 Required, Export Customers, Multiple Payment Accounts

Node.js 20 support has been dropped; v22.22.0 or later is now required. This release also ships customer CSV exports and support for multiple payment accounts in Medusa Payments.

CMS_BREAK -->

## Highlights

### Node.js v22.22.0 or Later Required

🚧 Breaking change

> This change only affects projects running Node.js 20. Projects already on Node.js 22 are unaffected.

Node.js 20 has reached end-of-life and is no longer supported. Medusa now requires Node.js v22.22.0 or later. Update your runtime environment before upgrading to this release.

```bash
node --version  # must print v22.22.0 or higher
```

[#17089](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17089)
[#17107](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17107)

---

## Configurable HTTP Query Params in Traced Spans

When instrumentation is enabled for HTTP requests, query parameters are now traced in the `url.query` property instead of the `http.url` property. Also, by default, only the values of the `fields`, `expand`, `limit`, `offset`, `order`, and `with_deleted` query parameters are displayed. Other values are traced as `REDACTED`.

You can configure this behavior by setting the `http.allowedQueryParams` option in the instrumentation settings:

```ts
export function register() {
  registerOtel({
    serviceName: "medusajs",
    exporter,
    instrument: {
      http: {
        // change allowed query param values
        allowedQueryParams: ["q", "limit", "offset"],
        // or to allow everything
        // allowedQueryParams: "*",
      },
      workflows: true,
      query: true,
      db: true,
      cache: true,
    },
  })
}
```

---

### Export Customers

Admin users can now export customer data as a CSV file directly from the dashboard. The export is backed by a new workflow and step in `@medusajs/core-flows`, a new admin API endpoint, and a new `admin.customers.export()` method in the JS SDK.

[#16142](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/16142)

---

### Multiple Payment Accounts for Medusa Payments

Medusa Payments now supports multiple payment provider accounts within the same project. This makes it possible to configure separate payment accounts per region or sales channel without running multiple Medusa instances.

[#17099](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17099)
